A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable methods, results, figures, tables, and extensive appendices. Content can be matched reliably across section moves and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on ten datasets, defense evaluations, human judgments, and calibration and pollution-ensemble analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds Binocular detection results and a sentiment-and-tone analysis of polluted evidence.

M1.justification: The thirteen pollution strategies, Table 1 prompts, and three defense procedures remain unchanged. Binocular extends the evaluated detector set without changing the proposed algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ten datasets across fake news, hate speech, rumor, and sarcasm detection, with the same pollution scenarios. The new attribute analysis examines existing Pheme pollution outputs.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds Binocular alongside DeBERTa and Fast-DetectGPT across eleven pollution strategies. FastGPT is renamed Fast-DetectGPT in the main text; its existing citation and implementation link establish that this is the same comparator.

E3.justification: Section 6 introduces a procedure using three-class sentiment and binary tone classifiers to characterize Pheme evidence. Existing splits, training settings, and defense evaluation protocols remain unchanged; the new metric appendix explains metrics already used.

E4.justification: New Figure 6 examines whether different pollution prompts produce distinct sentiment and tone distributions. Existing case studies, cross-distribution detection tests, calibration analyses, and pollution-ensemble experiments are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten-fold cross-validation, five runs per fold, and means with standard deviations for the main benchmark results. No changes to seeds, uncertainty estimation, or significance testing are documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds Binocular AUC/F1 results in Table 4, with a reported mean AUC of 80.1, and sentiment/tone findings in Figure 6. Tables 2–3 and the retained appendix results are unchanged. The parameter-updating discussion changes its exception from Reverse to Remove without changing the plotted results.

T1.justification: New Appendix B writes out the average-relative-score formula already described in v1's Table 3. This formalizes an existing calculation; the mathematical setup and method equations are retained, with no new theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims about pollution risks, limited defenses, calibration damage, and ensemble effects remain unchanged. Numerical highlights added to the abstract were already reported in v1, and the shortened conclusion preserves the contribution's scope.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds interpretations linking prompt wording to sentiment differences and spread-oriented generation to greater subjectivity. The Ethics Statement additionally recommends fact-checking evidence and explaining which evidence drives predictions. Existing scope limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project repository link and model links for the sentiment and tone classifiers. Appendix B clarifies metric computation and usage. Existing implementation settings are retained; the PDFs do not establish the linked repository's contents or accessibility.

R1.justification: Hans et al. (2024), introducing Binoculars, is newly cited and used in the detector comparison. The broader research positioning is retained; several other reference changes merely update existing preprints to publication details.

P1.justification: v2 separates general performance from pollution results, inserts a metric appendix, revises the abstract and conclusion, and updates affiliations and acknowledgements. Most prose and appendix organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Table 4 gains Binocular columns and revised category formatting, and Figure 6 adds sentiment/tone plots. Existing quality and calibration figures are reordered, with associated renumbering and reflow; retained appendix displays preserve their content.

improvement.justification: Adding Binocular makes the metric-based defense assessment less dependent on one detector, while Figure 6 provides targeted evidence about prompt-dependent output attributes. The metric appendix and resource links improve documentation. These are limited gains: the core evaluation is unchanged, Binocular settings remain unspecified, and Figure 3's caption still names Reverse despite the revised discussion naming Remove.
